notes: Minimal, facts-only ARK table. The ids are asset GUIDs from the game's own item database; display names are deliberately neutralised so no game text is redistributed. Run tools/extract_ark_ids.py against your own install for the full table with real names.

w0.name: socket_quality

values.4: WorldPatron (not accepted by the ark deserializer)

w0.note: ItemSocketQuality dataset index. The ark content deserializers only accept 1..3; any other value makes the record be dropped.

w1.name: socket_index
w1.note: 0-based ordinal of the socket inside the quality group. Counts come from the Ark asset ItemContainer.Sockets (A=1, B=2, C=3, WorldPatron=4).

w2.name: item_id
w2.note: 32-bit asset GUID of an Item asset (CBaseItem::GetID returns [obj+0xc], which is the id the item DB was queried with). Not in the table -> CInvalidItem -> slot renders empty/unknown.

w3.name: count
w3.note: size of the CItemStack id vector (item copies in the stack). 1 for a normal socketed item; 0 means 'empty slot' and is skipped by both readers and by the SetArk_V1 merge.
